column1: # Changes targum makes to STEP Bible's brief glosses (targum-internal#510).
# The glosses are the Gloss column of "TBESH - Translators Brief lexicon of Extended
# Strongs for Hebrew", www.STEPBible.org, based on work at Tyndale House Cambridge,
# CC BY 4.0, read at github.com/STEPBible/STEPBible-Data commit
# 48b7cfbda441adb6445ea565b4ed23dd98dfdf2e. Its licence lets us change the data and asks
# for a note of the changes that those who use it can see. This file is that note. The
# Meaning column (Abridged BDB, (c) Online Bible) is never read.
# Applied to every gloss, by rule (annotate/oshb.py, `shorten` and `briefs_from`):
# - Only the head is kept: the gloss up to its first ": ", so "to go: walk" is "to go".
# - "/" is written "; ", our gloss style, so "servant/slave" is "servant; slave".
# - Backticks and a closing "!" are taken off.
# - One gloss per Strong's number, as a card files it: where TBESH splits a number by
#   letter, the number takes the letter the Tanakh uses most, counted over the Open
#   Scriptures tagging, so 6213 is "to make" (6213a) and never "to press" (6213b).
# - The head of an entry is its row whose dStrong is its own uStrong with nothing after
#   the "=", else its first row that is not a name, else its first row.
# Changed by hand, one row each below. Columns: the eStrong number (a bare number is the
# one-gloss-per-number entry), the gloss the rules above give, the gloss we show, and why.

column4: the tagging files רָעָה as 7451c, so the count picks "distress", but the card is filed under רע and most of its tokens are the adjective
